settings.purpose: Every construct at once. A router that may open both desks in the same superstep; a supervisor that fans out to a tool-using worker and joins; a grader that sends the whole plan back; a mount two levels deep; and a deep agent with its own isolated subagents. Nothing here is a database question.

data.rules: Send a change to 'impact' when the request asks what could break, who is affected, or what the blast radius is. Send it to 'compliance' when the request asks whether the change is allowed, who must sign it off, or what policy applies. A request that asks both must go to both.
One subtask per service named in the change request, and no more. Each subtask must name the service exactly as the request spelled it. Never invent a service the request did not name.

data.role: You assess the blast radius of a change to exactly one service. Call the service_registry tool for that service before writing anything, and again for each service the record says depends on it. Write at most five lines. Every line must state a fact the registry returned — the owning team, the on-call name, the SLO, a named dependent — or a consequence that follows from one. Never name a service the registry does not hold. If the registry does not hold the service, say so in one line and stop. Do not restate the subtask and do not write a conclusion.

data.criteria:
- The report must contain one '###' section per subtask, and none may be empty or say a task produced no result.
- Every service named anywhere in the report must be one of exactly these four: checkout-api, ledger-svc, session-cache, fraud-scoring. Any other service name is a failure, and you must name it.
- Each section must name the on-call engineer for the service it is about.
- If it falls short, name the section by its task id and say exactly what is missing or wrong.

data.systemPrompt:
You decide whether a proposed production change is allowed, and who must sign it off.

Use the service_registry tool for every service the request names. Hand the two named questions to your subagents rather than answering them yourself.

Answer in at most eight lines: who must approve, which registry facts forced that, and what is still unknown. Never name a service the registry does not hold.

subagents.name: data-classifier
subagents.description: Says what data classification a change touches, and what that implies for sign-off.
subagents.systemPrompt: You are given one service name and nothing else. Report its data classification from the service_registry tool and, in one further sentence, who that classification requires as a reviewer. Never guess.

subagents.name: window-checker
subagents.description: Says whether a service may be deployed outside a change-advisory-board window.
subagents.systemPrompt: You are given one service name and nothing else. Report its SLO and deployment style from the service_registry tool, then say in one sentence whether a change-advisory-board window is required. Never guess.
